decisions.reason: Reopened GQ: the 'find humanity in everyone' line is printed in the closing paragraph as something she said about her drive to pick up the pieces after the show, not as an invitation policy. The paragraph built on it ('Her stated policy toward difficult people', 'That accounts for who was in the room') is gone and the quote was cut. No sentence states why she invited or kept anyone. The contradiction between her purpose and the jokes is now stated and left unexplained ('The Type 2 reading does not explain that'; 'The insult comedy is explained by none of them').

Reopened Dexerto (December 9, 2025). 'She has not disputed that criticism' is removed. The edit reports what Dexerto reports: a lot of the criticism was "really valid," 'without saying which parts'; the show is "much bigger than it used to be" and she has to "adjust for that"; and she defended her joke about Rakai's ban as understood in the room but not at home. The 'complimentary joke' line now carries GQ's lead-in ('Asked about her jokes before the show, she said she was working on it, he wrote'). Her and Fanfan's monologues are distinguished from Fanfan's Diddy comparison, and the racism and homophobia claims are attributed to 'unnamed posters' 'in GQ's summary of the feed'.

The Vice 'I've raised tons of money for charity' statement is not quoted or called a list, and 'it repeats the Vice interview' is gone. The deepfake section says 'Nor does it read her type from that stream', and none of the three Type 2 observations uses anything she said about the deepfakes. The repair cut the Type 3 section's separate sentence saying so, because the deepfake section already states it once. The Type 3 paragraph limits the tears to 'the tears over the 2025 backlash'. The Frost account says 'She did not uninvite him' (Dexerto: she 'shut down any notion of uninviting Frost').

Carried forward, then shortened at repair on the verifier's suggestion (verify-01, verify-04). 'The pattern ran small', 'grievance', 'The critics' point stands' and Ahgren's 'I hate them until I die' line were removed at the edit stage. The episode is now one dated sentence: 'On October 22, after the couple called out four late wedding guests on a podcast and viewers went after them, she posted: "This job is weird cause you share your personal life online and then as you become more ingrained in it other content creators become your personal life."' The quotation kept is her own explanation. The sentence states as fact what the critics pointed to (the couple called the guests out first), makes no ruling on it, and says nothing about the tone of the podcast remarks, so the 'did not hear the podcast' limit is no longer needed. One part of the test is met differently than at the edit stage: the critics' reply is no longer printed as an argument, and her answer to it went with it.

The author's verdict ('The complaint is not quite fair to them') is removed. The counterpoint is stated without fault: 'the surname is one she keeps private herself. No source opened here gives her reason', with the swattings and the BBC's account of men at her shop beside it and not claimed as her reason. GQ's 'hyperbolic' and Valkyrae's irritation stay in the preceding paragraph. The closing now reads 'By her own count in December 2025, an exaggeration even to the reporter who heard it'. meta_title is now "QTCinderella's Enneagram Type: She Says Nobody Knows Her". The October 2026 'other content creators become your personal life' quote is included as her later description of the same peers.

Reopened GQ. The childhood paragraph reads: 'Her parents were "mostly focused on getting divorced," she told GQ, though she also said they "definitely weren't neglectful."' The fragment is quoted without the abuse detail that follows it in GQ. Her mother's death is stated once in the biographical paragraph ('Her mother died in 2016.').

The sentence is kept (the enneagram reviewer protected it) and framed as one of two readings: 'That can be read two ways. She wants the effort seen and disowns the wish in the same sentence. Or, more plainly, she feels she has no standing to complain about an awards show.' The 'farm sympathy' quote was not added because GQ places it in the swatting passage, not the awards discussion.

Body: 'The reporting cited here presents no evidence of rigging. No vote counts are public either, so neither his claim nor her explanation can be checked from outside', with the panel caveat after it. FAQ: 'No evidence of rigging appears in the reporting reviewed for this profile, and QTCinderella denies it.' One part of the test could not be met as written: on reopening the coverage, the accusers are not only unnamed viewers. Dexerto (November 17, 2025) reports Asmongold accusing her by name of hand-picking nominees, so the body and FAQ name him; the broader 'rigged against right-wing streamers' claim stays attributed to 'some users' via GQ.

Opened Game Rant (February 12, 2024) directly: she ran the QTEvents channel herself to raise ad revenue, critics alleged a scam, and by her tweet the 41-minute ban followed an old video containing an explicit Omegle clip. The sentence and the word 'improvised' were then cut, which the test allows: a 41-minute platform ban is minor and the article was over the word ceiling. The source is kept as S27 and the episode is listed for the controversy file in research_tasks.

The deepfake section says 'GQ later described him as her "collaborator and friend."' (GQ: 'QT's collaborator and friend Brandon Ewing'). The forgiveness paragraph gives the plain non-type explanation: 'He was part of her working circle, so keeping away had a cost and forgiving had a practical use, whatever her type.' The OFFBRAND business tie is not printed because no opened source states it. The repair cut the lead-in 'He was not a stranger to her' as redundant with GQ's description.

The generalization about 'a person guarding an image' is cut. The edit names the norm ('Going live is how streamers answer a crisis, and Ewing's own apology that day was a live stream') and drops 'she goes live' from the Type 2 observations; the deepfake stream carries no type weight. Confidence wording stays medium.

Reopened Inven Global: it calls the Roast of Ludwig 'the first major event in QT's streaming career', so the draft's 'Sh*tcamp ... was the first large event she ran' was wrong and is corrected ('Her first major event, by Inven Global's account, was the Roast of Ludwig, an evening of insult comedy she organized for Ahgren'). The camera detail was cut for length, so the Roast is named in the event chronology instead. The through-line is stated ('her first major event was a roast') and the type read says outright that it does not explain her own jokes, twice ('The Type 2 reading does not explain that'; 'The insult comedy is explained by none of them').

The rigging FAQ now says 'Her partner won the top award at the first show in 2022, and she says she expected backlash for it.' The body section opens 'Doubts about the show's fairness are as old as the show' and states the 2022 win before the November 2025 dispute.

'Her mother died in 2016.' is in the biographical paragraph with no causal claim. The upbringing is restored from GQ ('GQ reported that her family was and remains in the Mormon Church, which she left at 18') and is used as a rival learned-practice explanation in the Type 3 section. That sentence was reworded at repair to stay inside her own words: 'A family and a church with a high bar for being good could also teach these habits to a child of any type'. The verifier found that 'prized service' was the editor's wording; in the recording she says she 'wasn't exactly holy' or 'perfect' and that she would 'never be good enough' for her father.

The edit shows the sequence that built her standing (a roast for Ahgren, then Sh*tcon, Sh*tcamp, the awards) and takes the test's second option for the objection: 'The skeptical view that her standing was borrowed from Ahgren's larger audience is not tested here.' The TSM exit is named in the same paragraph as unreviewed. A fuller sourced account of her 2020 to 2022 audience growth was not added; the article was over the word ceiling, and it is listed in research_tasks.

Roles are dated: 'The two people quoted praising her were her cohosts when they spoke, Higa at the 2022 awards and Valkyrae on the podcast in December 2025.' Wine About It is named in the biographical paragraph ('As of December 2025 she co-hosted the podcast Wine About It with Valkyrae'). The limits sentence now reads 'no named account of her motives, and no critical one, from a former collaborator, a crew member or anyone else who has worked with her', which stays true whatever Higa's later role. Higa's podcast history was not asserted because no opened source states it.

The Type 3 section gives each observation with its Type 3 answer ('each with a Type 3 answer'), now one short paragraph per observation: the 2020 account ('But it is one conversation, and "100%" is hers too'), the Frost list ('But a list of what she did is also a list of accomplishments'), and admiration versus thanks ('A Three can want thanks too').
